Updating clusters, worker nodes, and cluster components 

You can install updates to keep your Red Hat® OpenShift® on IBM Cloud® clusters up-to-date.

You must update your cluster by using the Red Hat OpenShift on IBM Cloud API, CLI, or console tools. You can't update your cluster version from OpenShift Container Platform tools such as the Red Hat OpenShift web console.



 Updating the master 

Periodically, Red Hat OpenShift releases [major, minor, or patch updates](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/openshift?topic=openshift-openshift_versions). Updates can affect the API server version or other components in your master. IBM updates the patch version, but you must update the master major and minor versions.



 About updating the master 

How do I know when to update the master?
: You are notified in the IBM Cloud console and CLI when updates are available, and can also check the [supported versions](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/openshift?topic=openshift-openshift_versions) page.

Can my worker nodes run a later version than the master?
: Your worker nodes can't run a later major.minor Kubernetes version than the master. Additionally, your worker nodes can only be one version behind the master version (n-1). First, [update your master](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/openshift?topic=openshift-updateupdate_master) to the latest Kubernetes version. Then, [update the worker nodes](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/openshift?topic=openshift-updateworker_node) in your cluster.

Worker nodes can run later patch versions than the master, such as patch versions that are specific to worker nodes for security updates.

How are patch updates applied?
: By default, patch updates for the master are applied automatically over the course of several days, so a master patch version might show up as available before it is applied to your master.

To update the cluster master, you can use the following command in the IBM Cloud CLI:

```bash
ibmcloud oc cluster master update --cluster CLUSTER [--version MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH] [--force-update] [-f] [-q]
```

Replace `CLUSTER` with the name or ID of your cluster. You can also specify the version you want to update to using the `--version` option. If you do not specify a version, the Kubernetes master will be updated to the default API version.

During the update, you won't be able to access or change the cluster, but your worker nodes, apps, and resources will continue to run without modification.

Make sure you have the necessary permissions, specifically the Operator platform access role for the cluster in IBM Cloud Kubernetes Service. After running the command, wait a few minutes and then confirm that the update is complete by checking the API server version on the IBM Cloud clusters dashboard or by running:

```bash
ibmcloud oc cluster ls
```

For more detailed instructions, you can refer to the IBM Cloud documentation.

To update the cluster master, you should follow these steps:
1. Check if your cluster is unsupported by reviewing the State field in the output of the `ibmcloud ks cluster ls` command or in the IBM Cloud Kubernetes Service console.
2. If your cluster is unsupported, you need to create a new cluster and deploy your apps to the new cluster. Then, you can delete the unsupported cluster.
3. Before updating to the latest version, make sure to update deprecated clusters to a supported version that is one or two behind the current version. For example, you can update to version 1.21 or 1.22 before updating to the latest version, 1.23.
4. If the worker nodes run a version two or more behind the master, update them to the same version as the master to avoid issues with your pods.
5. Finally, update the cluster using the instructions provided in the IBM Cloud documentation: <https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/containers?topic=containers-updateupdate>.
Keep in mind that updating a cluster to a new version may impact deployed apps, so it's essential to prepare accordingly.
CIS Kubernetes Benchmark

It is published by the Center for Internet Security (CIS). When a new Kubernetes version is released, IBM engineers compare the default configuration of a cluster that runs that Kubernetes version against the benchmark and publishes the results in the IBM Cloud documentation. The benchmark recommendations are provided by the Center for Internet Security, and it covers recommendations for master components, etcd, control plane configurations, worker nodes, and policies such as for users, network, and pod security.

1. Check if your cluster is unsupported by reviewing the State field in the output of the `ibmcloud ks cluster ls` command or in the IBM Cloud Kubernetes Service console.
